findings.title: Managed producer admits goal text rejected deterministically by the native stage validator after durable dispatch reservation
findings.criterion: Active increment contract line 13: overflow and unsupported forms refuse before reservation. Line 17: negative refusals leave the ledger/effects unchanged. Producer/native consumer grammar must agree before an otherwise-valid task enters one-shot uncertain dispatch.
findings.description: API text() bounds Python code points and calls clean_text(), which only rejects NUL/invalid encoding. The manifest goal is procedure.objective. Native entries() calls the shared native text(goal,4096), which instead bounds UTF-8 bytes and forbids C0/C1 controls and U+2028/U+2029. Consequently a short newline-containing objective, or 2100 U+00E9 characters (4200 UTF-8 bytes), passes the source Procedure/compiler/native package preparation and managed graph/brief/manifest producer but fails native validate_stage(). This is not an unsupported future slot/overlay feature.

reproducer.method: Copies only the synthetic b06b publication fixture into owned scratch; changes objective in copied YAML; compiles those source bytes; verifies native prepare_packages with exact file/digest list; validates a Procedure, builds managed records and validates the manifest; feeds its unchanged manifest into actual native stage validator. No DB/native process or mocks of these validators.
reproducer.positive_control: Ordinary ASCII objective is accepted by both producer and native validator.

findings.impact: prepare() persists the valid-by-API graph. NativeTaskOwner then commits reserve_dispatch(stage) BEFORE runtime.managed(task_stage). The deterministic downstream denial leaves stage_started=true with no binding; same-command stage is subsequently indeterminate and readback reports NEEDS_RECONCILIATION. That persistence consequence is traced from code, not independently replayed on PostgreSQL in this read-only review.
findings.minimal_fix: Validate the emitted manifest goal against the exact native stage grammar (UTF-8 byte cap and forbidden code points) during build/prepare before managed rows or dispatch intention are committed. Prefer a small shared/paired producer-contract guard with cross-layer tests; do not normalize/truncate the authored objective, widen authority, or retry an uncertain stage. Keep multiline source methodology text supported where it is not a wire goal.
findings.required_regression: Run the same ASCII positive and newline/UTF-8 negatives through the real qualified-publication/native-preparation/managed-prepare PostgreSQL path; negatives must refuse with unchanged managed ledger and no task_stage RPC. Keep a bounded non-ASCII positive within 4096 UTF-8 bytes. Re-review only the affected producer/wire fix and its tests.

findings.title: Managed producer accepts UTF-8 goals that the native wire refuses after dispatch reservation
findings.observed: Procedure objective of 2049 U+00E9 characters is accepted by Procedure.model_validate, build_records and domain.validate_manifest. It encodes to 4098 bytes; native validate_stage rejects it because text(goal,4096) uses UTF-8 bytes while domain text uses Python character count. The ordinary 19-character positive passes both. The rejected example produces a 37366-byte graph and 4865-byte manifest, within the documented overall graph and wire budgets.
findings.impact: The producer can materialize a valid-looking assignment that cannot be staged. In the real orchestration reserve_dispatch commits stage_started before RuntimeClient sends the request to RuntimeHost, where this stricter wire validation occurs; this can therefore become a sticky NEEDS_RECONCILIATION rather than pre-reservation rejection. This is an input-boundary correctness failure, not evidence of a model or target effect.

reproducer.expected: Every producer-admitted manifest passes the exact native stage validator, or producer refuses before reservation.
reproducer.boundary: Executed pure real producer and native wire validators, no DB. Sticky reservation consequence follows unchanged orchestration source; full PG reproduction not executed in this read-only review.

findings.violated_criterion: p2-b06b-managed-admission.md:13: overflow and unsupported forms refused before reservation; exact bounded stage protocol at lines15-17.
findings.minimal_remedy: Enforce the native goal UTF-8 bound/grammar and full stage payload bound at managed producer validation before durable prepare/reserve. Reuse a shared pure contract if practical; do not widen approved limits to hide mismatch. Add ASCII/multibyte boundary controls and a PG negative showing zero managed writes/dispatch for rejected input.

findings.title: Replacing the cold root revives a staged batch owned by a closed previous root
findings.observed: Stage under real cold AIAgent root A, close A, then replace the service resolver result with a distinct real cold AIAgent root B. stage(same manifest) returns A's old identities; release(original valid binding) returns BLOCKED and creates terminal results whose parent_session_id is the closed A. Leaving the resolver on the closed A correctly refuses. The batch stores no root object/session authority, and release only checks the currently resolved parent is not closed.
findings.impact: The new lifecycle extension does not fail closed on changed/unknown parent lineage. A new root can authorize old-root native records despite the documented closed-root denial. This is a service-level correctness/lineage counterexample, not a demonstrated exploit through the fixed RPC: the current managed_admission_rpc singleton does not itself rotate _ROOT, so ordinary installed RPC traffic does not presently trigger this transition.

reproducer.native_objects: Normal imports of full exported pin with exact six managed-source overlays; genuine AIAgent constructors, no dummy/object.__new__/method replacement.
reproducer.boundary: Full source-native host-interpreter probe, NOT installed Python3.13.15 or PG/UDS integration. Fresh private HOME/environment and audit refusal for network/subprocess/credential-file reads.

findings.violated_criterion: Contract line9 unknown lineage refused; managed-NOTICE.md:24-26 closed roots and unknown lineage refuse; delegated new-root-reuse review criterion.
findings.minimal_remedy: Bind each native batch to its original root object and immutable native/session identity. Require the same live root for stage replay that represents admission and for first release, under the registry lock; a distinct resolver root must not revive old pending children. Keep historical result readback receive-only. Add the old-closed/new-live-root positive/negative pair using genuine cold AIAgents.
